differences.what: massing from the plate's own camera: the front between the south gable at the left and the north corner block at the right, the round tower right of the gable under a slated cone with a finial, the very steep slated roof with iron cresting, and the north flank receding to the right; the front's two corners, the flank's rear corner, the tower's axis and the door land within 8.5 px of the plate (4.0 px RMS)
the tall stack rising off the north flank behind the corner block, standing where the plate draws it and to about its height

the storeys: with the cornice placed, the plate draws the chamber belt about 58 px (some 3 m) higher on the north corner than the record's 6.15 m and the walls' foot well above the record's grade, so it makes the walls about 0.8 of the record's height for their width; the row elevations (elevations_c1914_front) agree in direction, a principal storey near 4.8 m and a chamber storey near 3.6 m against the record's 4.3 and 4.35 m

the south gable: drawn as a tall stone wall gable rising through the roof with crockets, pinnacles and a finial, over a chamber pair and the arched pair of the principal floor (two round heads with colonnettes under one arch); built a low gable at the eave over square-headed pairs

the tower's top: the plate carries the tower a full stage over the main cornice, with its own lights and pinnacles, under a tall slated spire; the build springs a broader cone about 1 m over the cornice (the photograph's chicagology_photo record reads the cone lower still, so the two pictures, thirty years apart, are to be weighed against each other)

the dormers: the plate's are stone wall dormers with crocketed gables and pinnacles rising off the cornice, one over the north corner block and one on the north flank; built plain gabled dormers set in the slate
the entrance: the plate's door stands in a deep arched recess between carved capitals; built a flat-headed door at the stoop's head
the corbelled corner turret at the north corner block's flank corner (x 350-372, y 150-310 px of the cut, its corbel at y 310), with its little cone: not built
the low iron railing along the walk before the house
colour and the stone's tone: the plate is a monochrome engraving, so the brownstone's colour is not compared
the south flank, the rear and the roof's rear faces
the walk, the trees, the carriage and the figures, and the brick neighbour at the left
